  MINUTES
  VERNON BUSINESS AND INDUSTRY COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  THURSDAY, MAY 8, 2025
  COUNCIL CHAMBER, 4305 SANTA FE AVENUE

  CALL TO ORDER
  Chair Condon called the meeting to order at 9:03 a.m.

  FLAG SALUTE

  Chair Condon led the Flag Salute.

  ROLL CALL

  PRESENT:
  Thomas Condon, Chair
  Hector Morfin, Vice Chair
  Cathy Browne, Commissioner
  Paul Sablock, Commissioner
  Duncan Sachdeva, Commissioner

  ABSENT:
  Brian Bailey, Commissioner
  Melissa Ybarra, Commissioner

  STAFF PRESENT:
  Brian Saeki, City Administrator
  Zaynah Moussa, City Attorney (via remote participation)
  Genoveva Rocha, City Clerk

  None.

  May 8, 2025

  PRESENTATIONS
  1.  Fiscal Year 2025-26 Proposed Budget Overview
  Recommendation:
  No action required by Commission. This is a presentation only.
  City Administrator Saeki introduced the new City Clerk, Genoveva Rocha and newly
  appointed Finance Director Alice Hui to the Commissioners.

  City Administrator Saeki presented the staff report and accompanying PowerPoint
  presentation.
  In response to questions from the Commission, Staff provided additional information
  on the budget, they explained how staff defined transfers out of the electric fund and
  the costs for services such as payroll and benefits administration.

  Staff also provided the Commission with additional information on the budget for
  maintenance and operations, capital investment projects, utility transmission line, the
  addition of an additional water well, and prioritizing hydrant flushing as a lesson learned
  from the Eaton and Palisades fires.

  In response to the Commission’s questions on revenue impacts related to the data
  center and the loss of some major customers, VPU staff provided information on the
  City Council approval of the strategy to stabilize the billing component on customers’
  energy bill over three years, adding that along with the anticipated developments, the
  overall load will increase and in turn, increase the revenues.

  Commission members expressed concerns over increasing inflation rates, lower rental
  rates and calculations of the parcel tax as it relates to CPI and provided perspectives
  on vacancy rates, surcharges, warehousing vacancies, decreasing imports, increasing
  tariffs, parcel tax, and economic impacts surrounding warehousing in the City. The
  Commission requested a different look at options related to the calculations of the
  warehouse parcel tax.

  In response to concerns voiced by Commission members regarding whether the City's
  energy rate chart encompasses all fees and utility taxes, VPU staff provided information
  on comparative energy usage as it relates to other cities that have far greater residential
  customers and the unique and largely industrial base in Vernon.
  Vice Chair Morfin inquired about the City's fiscal responsibility concerning PFAS
  cleanups. City Administrator Saeki explained that the responsibility falls to each City
  while leveraging our State and Federal partners to help fund related projects. Public
  Utilities Assistant General Manager Otto shared that VPU closely monitors its drinking
  water for contaminants and has well monitoring.

  Chair Condon invited public comments. There being none, Agenda Item No. 2 was
  introduced.

  2.  Business License Tax
  Recommendation:
  No action required by Commission. This is a presentation only.

  City Administrator Saeki presented the staff report and Deputy City Treasurer Leon
  conducted a PowerPoint presentation.
  In response to Commission questions related to property square footage for business
  warehousing, Deputy City Treasurer Leon confirmed there is a cap on the business
  license tax and provided the average tax for the most recent annual renewal season
  was $5,777. It was clarified the average square footage per location, or user was
  calculated at approximately 24,000 square feet.

  The Commission members discussed the differences between manufacturing and
  warehousing, adding assembly to the process, shared some of the history of the
  warehouse tax which used to be miniscule and then presented challenges for business
  property owners once the tax was significantly increased. The Commission expressed
  interest in attracting new businesses to the City and thought it would help to simplify
  the tax calculation on the hybrid model.

  In response to a question on the definition of non-warehousing, Deputy City Treasurer
  Leon explained that the non-warehousing portion of a warehouse tax would include the
  area designated as office space, assembly area and staging and when an inspector
  visits the warehouse, the inspector would determine the square footage and then note
  the non-warehousing areas and consider the location’s unique situation.

  The Commission expressed concerns over the business tax on multiple locations, staff
  explained that according to business license records relating to the hybrid model, the
  City has two businesses that have four locations, two businesses that have three
  locations, and several businesses that have two locations. Staff explained there are
  factors that impact the calculations of business license tax depending on the type of
  license a business has.

  The Commission inquired about business tax on multiple adjacent locations compared
  to multiple non-adjacent locations, staff explained the business license tax is codified
  and to change the process would require approval by the City Council to take a ballot
  to the voters to amend the code.
  Police Chief Sousa provided information on copper wire theft in response to questions
  from the Commission.

  Chair Condon invited public comments.

  The Commission inquired and staff discussed and determined the average tax was
  $1,800 for businesses that were taxed based on the number of employees.

  There being no public comments or further discussion from the Commission, Chair
  Condon moved onto the Consent Calendar.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

  MOTION
  Vice Chair Morfin moved and Commissioner Sablock seconded a motion to approve
  the Consent Calendar. The question was called and the motion carried 5-0,
  Commissioners Bailey and Ybarra absent.
  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following item:
  3.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommendation: Approve the February 27, 2025 Special Business and Industry
  Commission Meeting Minutes.
  ORAL REPORTS
  4.  Brief Reports, Announcements, or Directives to Staff
  City Administrator Saeki announced the celebration of Professional Municipal Clerks
  Week and thanked the Vernon City Clerk's team for their hard work. He invited the
  community and encouraged Commissioners to join the business community on
  Wednesday, May 14th, at the Vernon Chamber of Commerce 2025 Economic Forecast
  and Industry Update Luncheon at Bridgepoint in Vernon. He stated speakers from U.S.
  Bank and L.A. Economic Development Corporation would provide an outlook on the
  regional labor market, global tariff climate and impacts on U.S. businesses and would
  provide the status of California and the regional economy.

  Lastly, he extended an invitation to the upcoming E-Waste Event in which Arion Global,
  and our Department of Health and Environmental Control would be co-hosting the
  annual electronic and universal waste recycling event at the Leonis Substation on 50th
  Street on Thursday, May 22nd from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. He encouraged all to
  support the effort to keep dangerous contaminants like lead, mercury and arsenic out
  of landfills and away from water supplies by recycling unused or obsolete electronics.

  ADJOURNMENT
  With no further business, Chair Condon adjourned the meeting at 10:28 a.m.
